name: Whisper large-v3-turbo
notes: ENCODER-DECODER, AND THIS IS THE MODEL WITH THE 4-LAYER DECODER. decoder_layers 4 vs 32 in large-v3 -- the whole point of turbo. ENCODER (unchanged, still the compute-heavy part): encoder_layers 32, d_model 1280, 20 heads, encoder_ffn_dim 5120, gelu, num_mel_bins 128, max_source_positions 1500. Identical to large-v3 and it DOMINATES the FLOPs: the 28 discarded decoder layers are ~0.73B of the 0.734B parameter reduction (1.543B -> 0.809B), and removing decoder layers removes decode work, NOT encoder work. DECODER: 4 layers, 20 heads, ffn 5120, max_target_positions 448. KV CACHE -- (a) DECODER SELF-ATTENTION, which is what kv_cache_bytes_per_token records: 4 layers * 20 kv_heads * 64 head_dim * 2 * 2 bytes (fp16) = 20,480 B/token = 20 KiB/token, exactly 1/8 of large-v3's 160 KiB because the layer count dropped 32 -> 4. (b) DECODER CROSS-ATTENTION over the 1,500 encoder frames, still CONSTANT per request: 4 * 20 * 64 * 1500 * 2 * 2 = 30,720,000 B = 29.3 MiB per in-flight request, exactly 1/8 of large-v3's 234 MiB. SO THE HEADLINE: turbo is ~2x faster end to end and uses ~8x less KV memory, but ONLY in the decode phase. The encoder -- >95% of the FLOPs for a typical 30s clip -- is bit-for-bit the same 32-layer pass. Anyone benchmarking turbo for throughput on short clips should expect a much smaller win than the 2x parameter reduction suggests, because the reduced part was never the bottleneck. The wins show up as lower time-to-first-token and as memory per concurrent request.  FIELD-PAIR WARNING for anyone deriving this from num_layers: num_layers is 32 here because it is the ENCODER depth, and the ENCODER HAS NO KV CACHE. The 4-layer figure that produces kv_cache_bytes_per_token is decoder_layers, a different config key. So the repo-standard derivation num_layers * num_kv_heads * head_dim * 2 * 2 would give 163,840 and be wrong by 8x for this record. whisper-large-v3 has no such trap precisely because its decoder is also 32 layers. STREAMING: still OFFLINE. The bidirectional 1,500-position encoder is unchanged from large-v3, so turbo inherits the same 30s buffering requirement. Turbo did not make Whisper streamable. flops_per_token_active is NULL, not 2*params -- see the reasoning in the whisper-large-v3 record; for an encoder-decoder that formula describes neither phase. params_b 0.809 = HF API safetensors total (808,878,080). License differs from large-v3: MIT here vs Apache-2.0 there.
